Iran parliament speaker says new regional pacts can 'herald a new stage’

Iran’s parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, has said that new regional treaties can herald a new stage in which Muslim neighbours rely on their own capacities rather than on foreigners, according to Tasnim News Agency.

In his message Saturday to mark the Unity Week, Ghalibaf described new regional treaties and arrangements as a “new chapter” and stressed that unity among Muslims has “helped push back against hegemonic ambitions”, according to Tasnim News Agency.

He said these treaties show that Muslim neighbours “can choose the path of cooperation and brotherhood”, rather than “pursuing exhausting rivalries”.

Ghalibaf added that recent developments have demonstrated the benefits of Muslim unity, and expressed hope that the Muslim world “would move toward greater unity, independence, security and dignity, with Muslims determining their own future free from foreign interference”.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Iran will stand firm against any aggressor, Pezeshkian says
item.description:
Iran will stand firm against any aggressor, Pezeshkian says

Iran’s president Masoud Pezeshkian said Tehran does not seek war but will stand firmly against any aggressor, stressing that no power can force a nation determined to resist to surrender.

“The Islamic Republic of Iran is not the initiator of war,” he said, adding, “we do not welcome war, but we will stand firmly against any aggressor with strength, and no power can force a nation that is standing with all its strength and determination to surrender.”

Pezeshkian said Iran would not bow to threats as it has the backing of diplomatic efforts, the support of the Iranian people, the work of government officials and the sacrifices of commanders of the armed forces.

“We will not bow our heads before any threat, just as we have demonstrated many times before,” he said.

Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi, meanwhile, said the Strait of Hormuz remains closed and any ship can pass through it only with the permission of Iran.

“The Iranian armed forces have complete oversight over movements in the Strait of Hormuz, and we do not confirm the claims regarding the uncoordinated passage of ships,” he said.

Asked about attempts by mediators Pakistan and Qatar to revive the talks, he said: "We have clarified to Qatar and Pakistan the steps the United States should take.” 

“America is the one that violated all its commitments in the Memorandum of Understanding, and it is the one that must implement these commitments,” he told reporters on Saturday.

Regarding the management of the Strait of Hormuz, he said, necessary arrangements have been made with the government of Oman.

“Whenever these commitments are fulfilled, Iran will take the necessary actions,” he said.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Amnesty calls for Dr Abu Safiya's release as he completes 600 days in Israeli detention
item.description:
Amnesty calls for Dr Abu Safiya's release as he completes 600 days in Israeli detention

Amnesty International has called for the release of Palestinian paediatrician Hussam Abu Safiya, who has completed 600 days in Israeli detention.

Abu Safiya, director of Gaza’s Kamal Adwan Hospital, rose to international prominence during Israel's genocide due to his role in helping victims.

He was abducted by Israel on 27 December 2024 and has been held without charge or trial since. 

“He is still being held without charge, separated from his family, his colleagues, and the children he lovingly treated,” Amnesty International said in a statement.

“Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya stood at the centre of Kamal Adwan Hospital as Gaza's healthcare system collapsed around him. Day in, day out, he treated his patients and carried out his medical duties, working through unbearable loss and grief. He bore witness to the devastating toll of Israel's ongoing genocide in Gaza,” the statement read.

Throughout this time, Abu Safiya, like numerous Palestinian healthcare workers, refused to abandon his patients. 

“He stayed at the hospital until the last second when Israeli forces raided it again and arbitrarily arrested him on 27 December 2024,” the statement said.

In July, more than 800 doctors, nurses and medical professionals in the UK signed an open letter to foreign secretary Yvette Cooper, calling for her urgent intervention to secure the release of Abu Safiya.

Egyptian foreign minister Badr Abdelatty and his Kuwaiti counterpart Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah called for de-escalation and a return to diplomacy and negotiations between Iran and the United States during a phone call, according to Egypt's Foreign Ministry.

The two ministers discussed rapidly evolving regional developments and ways to contain the current escalation, the Egyptian ministry said in a statement.

They agreed that de-escalation and the resumption of negotiations between Iran and the United States should be a priority, highlighting the memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed by Iran and the United States on June 18 as a framework to restart talks and reach political solutions that could spare the region further tension and instability, it added.

The ministers also exchanged views on regional security concerns and called for addressing all sources of tension in ways that promote regional security and stability, the statement said.

Under the MoU to end the war in the region, Tehran and Washington were scheduled to hold negotiations within 60 days, which ended on Aug. 17, to reach a final agreement. The fate of the talks remains unclear following the escalation between the two countries last month. (Reporting by Reuters)

item.description:
Israeli forces, settlers killed 235 children in West Bank since 7 Oct 2023, report says

Israeli forces have killed 235 children and teenagers, including a seventh-month-old infant, in West Bank since 7 October 2023, AFP reported. 

The killing of Palestinian children and teenagers by Israel in the West Bank has become increasingly common since the start of the war in Gaza, the report said.

Five of the 235 children have been killed by Israeli settlers, according to B'Tselem, an Israeli rights group.

The Palestinian Authority's Colonisation and Wall Resistance Commission, a Palestinian government institution, reported 250 such deaths over the same time period.

In the 17 years between 2005 and 2021, an average of roughly one Palestinian child or teenager was killed by Israeli forces every month, according to B'Tselem, a frequent but much lower rate.

For the period since the October 7 attack, the average using B'Tselem figures is around seven killed per month, the report said.

Last year, of the 54 Palestinian children or teenagers killed according to B'Tselem, the youngest was just two years old, while the majority were aged between 14 and 17.

In several other cases, the army has fired indiscriminately at Palestinians and killed children who were present.

One such casualty was seven-month-old Sam Abu Haikal, shot in the face by Israeli troops in the West Bank city of Hebron in June 2026.

His mother, Dania Abu Haikal, 28, told AFP she was also wounded when the troops fired at their car while Sam was on her lap, with a bullet entering through her cheek and exiting through her ear.

She bore a large scar on her face when she met with AFP at her home in Bethlehem, holding a stuffed fox that had belonged to her son.

"Why would anyone shoot an infant? What did a little baby, a seven-month-old infant, do to harm the soldiers?" Abu Haikal, a university lecturer, told AFP.

item.description:
Israel, US 'sworn enemies of Muslim unity', Mojtaba Khamenei says

Iran’s supreme leader, Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei, has described the United States and the Israeli regime as “sworn enemies” of unity among Muslims, stressing the need for greater solidarity and cooperation across the Islamic world.

In his written statement released Sunday, Mojtaba Khamenei said, the US and Israel “strive to turn various racial, cultural, social, economic, political, and geographical differences into pretexts for creating discord among Muslim people in Iran and in any other Islamic country”.

“From this perspective, they observe the fragmentation of the Islamic Ummah and the weakening of its forces, waiting for the opportune moment to impose their dominance over them,” the statement said, according to Al Jazzera.

Khamenei asked "would the Palestinian nation be so defenceless, subjected to the oppression and crimes of the occupiers, if Muslims were united, clenching their fists with strength?” 

“And would the nations and governments residing around the Persian Gulf have the courage to let corrupt and identity-less scoundrels from thousands of kilometres away covet their lands and assets if they established their unity under the banner of Islam?”

He urged Muslim heads of state to “recognise their real enemy, understand its plans, and confront it”.

“The criminal rulers of America and the fake Zionist regime are sworn enemies of this unity and friendship,” said Khamenei.

“They are not only enemies of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation, as well as the vast front of Islamic resistance; they also harbour animosity towards the entire Muslim Ummah, including the nations of West Asia and North Africa,” the statement said.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Sudanese in Kordofan's Bara the latest civilians to be forced into battle
item.description:
Sudanese in Kordofan's Bara the latest civilians to be forced into battle

Submitted by Mohammed Amin on Fri, 08/28/2026 - 16:26
The Popular Resistance has played a crucial role in battlefield successes against the RSF, but some claim it is a vehicle to return figures from the Bashir era
Members of the pro-Sudanese army Popular Resistance group gather for a rally in the Karary district of Omdurman on 30 June 2026 (Ebrahim Hamid/AFP)
Off

From the Sudanese war’s earliest months, civilians have been forced to take up arms to defend themselves.

In Darfur’s al-Geneina in the summer of 2023, members of the Masalit community fought back as the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and allied militias rampaged through the city.

Similarly, villages in al-Jazira state south of Khartoum fought off invading paramilitaries as communities around them were overrun.

And in el-Fasher, the North Darfur state capital that was under siege for over 550 days, residents helped keep the RSF at bay until the defensive lines finally collapsed in October 2025, precipitating the massacre of an estimated 60,000 people.

Since then, the focus of the war has shifted to Kordofan, the resource-rich region to the south.

Here, too, civilians have taken up arms, most often part of the Popular Resistance units fighting alongside the Sudanese Armed Forces, but also through non-violent means.

The Popular Resistance was established by army chief General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan in June 2023, with the SAF providing tens of thousands of civilians with weapons and training.

Its cadres include people from all parts of Sudanese society, including pro-democracy revolutionaries who previously opposed Burhan and his military rule.

However, Sumood, the bloc of civilian political parties led by former prime minister Abdalla Hamdok, argues that the Popular Resistance is dominated by religious conservatives who intend to use it to return figures from Omar al-Bashir’s era to power.

In North Kordofan, the scene of intense recent battles, Popular Resistance fighters say politics has taken a back seat when confronted with the danger of the RSF.

Mustafa Karam al-Din, a pharmacist from the city of Bara, joined the Popular Resistance under SAF command when the RSF killed his brother and ransacked his home last year.

“They raided our house, killing my brother and others in my neighbourhood, so I had no option other than taking up weapons to protect myself and my family and neighbours,” he tells MEE in el-Obeid, the North Kordofan state capital.

“The RSF was very brutal with everybody when they entered the city. That wasn't just against armed people but against all citizens, including the civilians.”

According to Karam al-Din, the RSF was out for revenge when they recaptured Bara, after the SAF briefly held the city last year, because its residents had celebrated the paramilitary's ouster.

“They had videos and lists of some people, including the agents of the Popular Resistance,” he says.

Karam al-Din says it became clear to civilians in Bara and elsewhere in Kordofan that they needed to protect themselves.

“They entered police stations and weapons stores and took up weapons. They also got others from the SAF. Then the Popular Resistance was organised, including in Bara, el-Obeid and other areas in Kordofan,” he said.

Bara, in particular, has witnessed extreme violence. The RSF and SAF have traded the city on Kordofan’s strategic Export Road several times over the past three years. Since July, Bara has been held by the army.

“Since October last year we have been fighting with the SAF against the RSF until we liberated our city, and I’m very proud of that,” Karam al-Din says.

The RSF has committed abuses across Sudan since the war broke out and has been accused of genocide in Darfur by the United States and several human rights groups.

'This conflict has become a war against the UAE’s foreign invasion, which is using the RSF as a tool'

- Mustafa Karam al-Din, Popular Resistance fighter

The group is backed by the UAE, which despite global outrage has supplied the paramilitary with weapons and mercenaries.

“This conflict has become a war against the UAE’s foreign invasion, which is using the RSF as a tool,” says Karam al-Din, who currently mans checkpoints on the frontline.

According to him, weapons and other supplies from the UAE were found in the hands of RSF fighters as the SAF retook Bara.

“We have also arrested mercenaries from Colombia, South Sudan and other countries fighting with the RSF in Um Syala and Gabrat al-Shiekh,” he says.

Godat Abdul Hadi, a leading member of the Popular Resistance, told MEE that it provides military training for hundreds of youths from Bara who were displaced to el-Obeid.

“The Popular Resistance in el-Obeid, Bara and other areas began at the start of the war and even before the SAF officially declared and expanded it under SAF command,” he says.

“The number was initially small, but it has hugely increased in response to the RSF invasion of the majority of North and West Kordofan and with the widespread atrocities it committed.”

Protection and risk

When the RSF attacked Bara last October, Mohammed Adam was sitting with his friends and neighbours, talking about the humanitarian efforts to help Bara’s people after the paramilitary’s last devastating assault.

Despite some of his friends and cousins carrying weapons, Adam, who is a pro-democracy activist and part of the Resistance Committees network that led the 2019 popular revolution against Bashir, was not convinced carrying weapons alongside the SAF was the right solution to the danger of the RSF.

When the RSF overran his city, any evidence that civilians were involved in armed resistance was a death sentence for people trying to flee.

In Sudan’s deserted Bara, blood waters its famous lemon trees
Read More »

“I can never forget that day. Some of the armed youths were with me in my house, and they were unable to join their units because of intensive RSF fire. So, we lay under beds for hours, and when the crossfire stopped, we realised the SAF had been defeated and RSF fighters were starting to attack civilians,” he recalls.

“We quickly decided to hide everything associated with fighting, including my friends’ Kalashnikovs and military uniforms. I gave them some of my normal clothes, and we decided to leave the city that day.”

Before they could leave, RSF fighters entered Adam’s house and threatened everyone there, accusing them of being "fulool", a term for people associated with the “deep state”. Despite searching the home, fortunately they did not uncover the guns and fatigues.

That night, Adam and his friends were able to escape Bara and head towards el-Obeid, which was still under SAF control.

“When we got out of my house, we saw a disaster. Dozens of dead bodies were in the streets, and wounded and displaced people were all along the route. The people of the nearby villages helped us with whatever they could provide: food, water and simple medical treatment,” he says.

“We endured difficult times at the hands of the RSF. One incident turned the people of Bara against them completely, when they killed one of our neighbours and then attacked the funeral ceremony the same day, killing many other people for no reason.”

Skeptics among the revolutionaries

Not all of Kordofan’s pro-democracy activists are so supportive of the Popular Resistance.

One member of the Resistance Committees network in Bara told MEE he believes that the mobilised units are dominated by religious conservatives and people linked to Bashir’s rule.

“Former regime associates are leading the so-called Popular Resistance in Bara and other places in order to pave the way for the old regime to exploit the war and return to power,” says the activist, who asked for anonymity for security reasons.

“This war has to be stopped by all means and concessions. It destroyed the country and enabled the old regime to come back through the SAF,” he claims.

However, Adam said many Sudanese, particularly the youth, don’t feel like they have a choice whether to take up arms and fight under SAF command or not.

“The RSF has attacked everybody: civilians or military, young or old, men or women. They take revenge on everybody in Bara,” he says.

“Those who took up weapons in self-defence were our brothers, cousins and neighbours. Any previous political disagreements are not an issue at the moment,” he adds.

“Let me tell you: I prefer not to carry weapons under the SAF, but I can’t tell those who have been attacked and humiliated by the RSF not to defend themselves by all means.”

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] NBC journalists attacked as settler violence continues across occupied West Bank
item.description:
NBC journalists attacked as settler violence continues across occupied West Bank

Men wearing masks attacked an NBC News television crew near the occupied West Bank village of Jalud while the journalists were interviewing a Palestinian woman who said she had been driven from her home by Israeli settlers, Palestinian news agency Wafa reported. 

The incident comes amid a wider escalation of settler violence across the occupied territory.

Israeli forces also bulldozed Palestinian-owned land in Deir Ballut, while hundreds of settlers, accompanied by Israeli forces, raided Islamic religious sites in Awarta, local media said. 

Two elderly sisters were wounded in an alleged settler assault in Silwad on Saturday, while attacks and raids were also reported overnight in Arrabeh, al-Mughayyir, Burqa, Masafer Yatta, Khallet al-Hummus, Yasouf, Khalayel al-Louz and Nablus.
